title: People’s Mañanera August 27
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**National Sovereignty Above All Other Interests  
** President Claudia Sheinbaum will propose a bill requiring candidates for
the presidency, state governors, and the Head of the Mexico City Government to
hold only Mexican citizenship or renounce any other. The goal is “for the
nation’s interest to take precedence over any other,” she explained.

**A Candidacy Launched from Another Country  
** Regarding the presidential aspirations of former Tamaulipas governor
Francisco Garcia Cabeza de Vaca, the President quipped that “it’s very
difficult to be a candidate and launch that campaign from another country,
isn’t it?”. Cabeza de Vaca lives in Texas.

**Mexico Does Not Abandon Its Compatriots  
** In response to the deaths of Mexican nationals in ICE custody, the
government filed complaints and demanded a full investigation. Sheinbaum asked
the Ministry of Foreign Relations to press Marco Rubio on the issue. “We do
not agree with the treatment our Mexican brothers and sisters are receiving,”
the President explained.

**Mexico Does Not Belong to Any Political Party  
** The President backed the resolution calling for Somos México, which seeks
its registration as a new political party, to change its name, emblem, and
colors. No political party can appropriate the national identity, she said,
pointing out the contradiction the opposition faces. “Previously, they
demanded that the National Electoral Institute (INE) remain untouched, and now
they’re using the INE’s colors.”

**La Derecha Diario: Lies and Foreign Interference  
** Sheinbaum revealed that right-wing ideologue Fernando Cerimedo was a
partner at La Derecha Diario when he was arrested in Bolivia, despite owner
Javier Negre’s denial, and added that the media outlet “has sought to
interfere in Mexican politics from abroad.”

**Audience Rights, Without Censorship  
** The new guidelines will ensure codes of ethics, audience ombudsmen, and
effective complaint submission mechanisms, without penalizing content or
opinions. The President was clear. We have always fought for freedom of
expression, she said.
